evaluated.name: Improving Profits With Earned Capital
evaluated.hypothesis: An upward trend in operating profitability is credible when the firm has a deep stock of retained earnings, since cumulative internally generated capital verifies that past profits were real and reinvestable rather than one-time or externally financed.
evaluated.reasoning: TREND captures the profitability-improvement channel while retained earnings over assets is a balance-sheet quality/maturity measure of accumulated earnings history, so the pair distinguishes a genuine profitability ramp from a fragile turnaround at a capital-depleted firm. Neither leg alone contains this validation logic: young cash-burning firms can trend upward from a very low base, and mature high-RE firms can be stagnant. The rank combination keeps both channels on a comparable scale and preserves broad coverage.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Interest Adjusted Profit With Debt Coverage
evaluated.hypothesis: Profitability net of the cost of debt, combined with the ability of operating cash flow to service total liabilities, isolates operating strength that belongs to shareholders rather than profitability that is manufactured or claimed by leverage.
evaluated.reasoning: The first rank is a profitability spread after financing costs (profitability theme adjusted for the capital structure claim) and the second is a cash-flow-to-liabilities solvency ratio (quality theme), so the product is high only when profits survive interest and cash flow comfortably covers obligations. This penalizes the classic levered-ROE illusion, where high equity returns simply reflect debt amplification. It should produce a long leg of unlevered, cash-generative compounders and a short leg of levered, cash-poor firms.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Profits Not Propped By New Debt
evaluated.hypothesis: Sustained operating profitability accompanied by shrinking or flat debt reflects genuine internal cash generation, while equally high reported profitability alongside rapid new borrowing signals profits being financed and flattered by balance-sheet expansion that will reverse.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a flow rather than a level mechanism: it conditions the profitability state on the direction of debt financing over the past year, so it separates self-funding operators from firms whose apparent strength coincides with creditor support. The three-year moving average removes single-year profit noise without imposing the coverage cost of a five-year window. It tests a financing-flow channel that neither gen-0 survivor examined.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Working Capital Backed Profitability
evaluated.hypothesis: High operating profitability is more likely to persist when the firm holds enough net working capital relative to its total obligations to fund the operating cycle internally, since liquidity-constrained profitable firms must divert operating cash to near-term claims rather than to shareholders.
evaluated.reasoning: This is the graded repair of the gen-0 binary solvency gate: net working capital scaled by total liabilities enters as a continuous rank, so firms are ordered smoothly by liquidity instead of being dumped en masse into the short leg, which prevents the spread from degenerating into a pure distress bet. Both legs use high-coverage annual items and no time window at all, so it should have the broadest coverage in this batch. It isolates the liquidity channel of financial health, separate from the debt-level channel in Signal 1.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Total Leverage Discounted Profitability
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), RANK(NEG(MUL(RATIO(xsga, sale), RATIO(lt, at)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Profitability is fragile when the firm carries both high fixed operating costs and high financial obligations, because the combined operating-and-financial leverage converts modest revenue shortfalls into large earnings declines; the same profitability at a low-total-leverage firm is far more likely to persist.
evaluated.reasoning: The penalty term multiplies an operating-rigidity proxy (SG&A intensity of sales, a profitability-theme item) by a solvency proxy (total liabilities over assets, a quality-theme item), so it captures the compounding of the two leverages rather than either one in isolation. This is a genuinely different mechanism from simple debt-level conditioning: it predicts that fixed-cost-heavy firms need clean balance sheets for their profits to be durable. Both inputs are broadly reported, and the rank product keeps the signal bounded and monotone in each leg.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Rollover Risk Adjusted Profitability
evaluated.hypothesis: What makes profitability fragile is not the amount of debt but its maturity: a profitable firm whose claims are concentrated in debt due within a year must keep refinancing at the mercy of credit markets, so its operating strength is hostage to rollover conditions, while the same profitability financed with long-dated or non-debt claims is insulated.
evaluated.reasoning: The quality leg is the short-term share of the liability structure, which is orthogonal by construction to the leverage level used in Quality-Minus-Junk safety, so this tests maturity composition rather than rediscovering profitability-plus-low-leverage. The interaction is the point: refinancing risk should erode the value of high operating profitability far more than it matters for firms with little profit to protect, and the rank product concentrates the long leg on profitable firms with term-funded balance sheets. Scaling short-term debt by total liabilities rather than assets keeps the measure defined for debt-free firms and avoids simply re-expressing total leverage.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Distribution Verified Profitability
evaluated.hypothesis: Reported profits are credible when the firm actually hands cash to shareholders; using the retained-earnings identity, income not added to retained earnings is the payout, so profitability accompanied by real distributions reflects durable earning power rather than accounting income that can only ever be reinvested or written off.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the retained-earnings *stock* channel of the archived signal and instead uses the year-over-year retained-earnings identity to back out implied distributions, a verification mechanism that is economically distinct from a level of accumulated earned capital. The interaction matters because a payout is uninformative at an unprofitable firm and is precisely the hard-cash confirmation that separates durable from paper profitability at a profitable one. Both inputs are widely reported and only a one-year lag is required, so coverage should remain high.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Stable Financing Durable Profits
evaluated.hypothesis: A firm with genuinely durable operating strength does not have to keep re-levering and de-levering to fund itself, so an erratic liability-to-assets path reveals funding dependence and earnings fragility even when the current profitability level looks strong.
evaluated.reasoning: Replacing the F-score's Δleverage and Δliquidity indicators with the *volatility* of the capital-structure path changes the economic object from a one-year directional improvement to the stability of the financing model, which is not a published score component and cannot be captured by any single-year change. The multiplicative rank form gives each leg equal weight, fixing the silent double-weighting of the nested SUMRANK, and the four-year volatility window is short enough to preserve reasonable coverage. The prediction is a joint one: financing stability should be rewarded mainly where there are substantial profits to sustain.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Profit Coverage Of Near Term Claims
evaluated.hypothesis: The relevant measure of durable operating strength is how many times current-year operating profit covers the claims coming due within the year; a firm whose annual EBITDA dwarfs its current liabilities is structurally insulated, while an equally profitable firm whose near-term claims exceed its profit stream is one bad year from creditor control.
evaluated.reasoning: The two archive winners both scale a claim measure by total liabilities and then rank-multiply with profitability; this proposal collapses the same economics into a single credit-style coverage ratio, which lets us learn whether the payoff comes from the interaction structure or simply from measuring profit relative to imminent obligations. Industry adjustment is essential because current-liability intensity is highly sector-dependent (retail and utilities versus software), so the raw ratio would otherwise sort industries rather than firms. Both inputs are among the best-populated annual items, so coverage should be at the high end of the archive.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Funding Pressure Adjusted Profitability
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt), NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Liquidity buffers and debt-maturity structure are two separable dimensions of near-term funding pressure, and profitability is most durable when both are favourable: liquid resources cover the operating cycle *and* little of the liability stack must be refinanced immediately.
evaluated.reasoning: This directly tests whether the two independently successful quality legs are complementary or redundant — if the combined score beats both parents on alpha and t-statistic, funding pressure is genuinely multi-dimensional; if it merely matches them, the legs are proxies for one another and later generations should stop adding balance-sheet channels. The inner SUMRANK equalises the weight of the liquidity and maturity legs before they gate profitability, avoiding the silent double-weighting problem flagged earlier. Coverage should match the parents since all four inputs are standard balance-sheet items.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Profits Without Payables Stretch
evaluated.hypothesis: A profitable firm that is quietly financing itself by letting current liabilities outrun its sales base is converting supplier and accrual credit into reported operating strength; that funding source is finite and reversible, so such profitability is less durable than profitability generated with a stable trade-credit position.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a different failure mode from the interest-bearing debt-growth flow that produced negative alpha in gen 1 — trade credit and accrued obligations are not capital-market financing, and stretching them is a documented precursor of operating strain rather than a deliberate leverage decision. Benchmarking current-liability growth against contemporaneous sales growth removes the mechanical scaling that made the raw debt-growth leg behave like a size-and-investment tilt. It gives the batch one genuine flow mechanism to sit alongside the level-based consolidation, so we learn whether *any* flow variable can work in this theme pair or whether only levels do.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Habitually Liquid Profitable Firms
evaluated.hypothesis: A liquidity buffer is a policy, not an accident: firms that have maintained positive net working capital in every one of the last five years have demonstrated an institutionalised commitment to self-funding their operating cycle, and their current profitability is therefore far more likely to survive a demand or credit shock than the profitability of a firm that only happens to be liquid this year.
evaluated.reasoning: This is not smoothing — it replaces the magnitude of the balance-sheet leg with a count of how many years the solvency condition actually held, which is a track-record concept that no moving average can express and which the two failed MA signals therefore did not test. The count is coarse and outlier-immune, so unlike the level-based liquidity leg it cannot be driven by a handful of cash-hoarding observations, and ranking it before multiplication keeps both legs bounded with no zero-crossing pathology. It also tells us something decision-relevant: whether the archive's liquidity payoff comes from the current buffer size or from a persistent financial policy.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Implied Borrowing Rate Discount
evaluated.hypothesis: The rate lenders actually charge is an informed external verdict on earnings durability, so among borrowers, high operating profitability obtained at a low effective interest rate reflects credit-market confirmation of the franchise, while the same profitability funded at a punitive rate signals that specialists with access to private information regard the profits as fragile.
evaluated.reasoning: Scaling interest expense by interest-bearing debt rather than by total liabilities makes the measure an actual price per unit of borrowing instead of a disguised debt-mix ratio, which is exactly the confound the critic identified; the debt-composition channel is then no longer mechanically embedded in the leg. Winsorising the ratio controls the small-denominator explosions that arise for firms with trivial debt balances, and firms with no debt simply drop out, which is economically correct because there is no lender verdict to observe. Coverage will be the key diagnostic on whether creditor-priced information can be used at all in this theme pair.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Trough Profit Cover Of Current Claims
evaluated.hypothesis: Financial durability should be assessed under stress: the right question is not whether this year's profit covers claims coming due, but whether the firm's *worst* operating profit of the recent past would still have covered them, since that is the state in which creditors force asset sales or dilutive financing.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces a functional-form tweak with a genuinely new economic object — a self-referential stress test that crosses the firm's own historical downside in operating profit with the size of its near-term obligations — and it is not a monotone transform of any archive signal because two firms with identical current coverage can differ sharply in their trough coverage. Industry adjustment is necessary because both the cyclicality of EBITDA and the intensity of current liabilities are sector traits, so the raw ratio would sort industries rather than firms. Using a minimum rather than a mean or standard deviation keeps the emphasis on downside survivability, which is the part of stability that creditors and equity holders actually care about.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Rollover Need Versus Liquid Resources
evaluated.hypothesis: Refinancing risk is not about how much of the liability stack is short-dated but about whether liquid resources already on hand can retire the maturing debt; a profitable firm whose current assets far exceed its short-term debt faces no rollover decision at all, whereas one with the same maturity mix but thin liquid assets must return to lenders on their terms.
evaluated.reasoning: This changes the economics of the winning leg rather than its form: dlc/lt measures the composition of claims, while dlc/act measures whether the firm can self-retire those claims, which is the mechanism the rollover story actually invokes. It also unifies the two independently successful quality legs (liquidity and maturity) into a single asset-versus-obligation comparison instead of blending their ranks, which is a substantively different aggregation from gen-2's SUMRANK merge. Both inputs are dense, so coverage should be at the top of the archive range.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Within Industry Profit And Maturity
evaluated.hypothesis: Both operating profitability and reliance on short-term debt are heavily sector-determined, so the priced information should be a firm's standing relative to its industry peers rather than its position in the pooled cross-section; industry-neutral scoring should raise abnormal returns by stripping out sector bets that FF5 factors partly absorb.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a conditioning-set experiment on the best archive signal, not a formula tweak: pooled ranks let capital-intensive, short-debt-heavy industries populate the short leg wholesale, which produces industry rather than firm selection and can inflate factor loadings while diluting alpha. Industry-relative ranking preserves the exact economic interaction while enforcing peer comparability, and the earlier IND_ADJ result is uninformative here because that signal also abandoned the rank-product structure. A clear improvement would tell later generations to industry-neutralise both legs by default.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Profit Volatility Against Obligations
evaluated.hypothesis: Fragility arises when the variability of the profit stream is large relative to the obligations that must be paid regardless of business conditions; a firm whose EBITDA fluctuates by a small fraction of its current liabilities can always service them, while equal profitability with fluctuations comparable to its near-term claims implies a real probability of a funding shortfall.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive's volatility failure used the volatility of the capital structure itself, which is a financing-policy artefact; here the second moment is applied to the profit stream and is scaled by the obligations it must cover, making it a crude distance-to-distress rather than a stability anomaly. This is the only construction in the batch in which the two themes interact inside a single quantity, and it tests whether cash-flow risk relative to claims adds anything beyond the static claim structure. The five-year window is affordable given that comparable windows have cost the archive little coverage.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Rising Short Debt Reliance Penalty
evaluated.hypothesis: A profitable firm that is actively shifting its funding toward short-dated debt is revealing either loss of access to term credit or a deliberate bet on refinancing conditions, and that migration predicts deterioration in the durability of its profits even before the level of short-term debt looks alarming.
evaluated.reasoning: Flow constructions have failed twice, but both used aggregate debt or trade-credit growth, which are contaminated by investment and size effects; this applies the change operator to the *specific ratio* that has produced the archive's most reliable alpha, so a null result cleanly establishes that this channel is a level effect and closes off flow variants for good. If instead it works, it identifies a faster-moving, higher-turnover version of the winning mechanism with distinct timing. The construction is bounded, uses only dense items, and requires a single lag.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Pricing Power With Term Funding
evaluated.hypothesis: Durable operating strength shows up as pricing power — profit per dollar of revenue after depreciation — rather than as profit per dollar of assets, and pricing power is only bankable for equity holders when the firm is not forced to renegotiate its funding each year; margin-strong firms with term-funded balance sheets can defend prices through downturns instead of discounting to raise cash.
evaluated.reasoning: Switching the scaler from assets to sales changes the economic object rather than restating it: asset-scaled profitability is the product of margin and asset turnover, and only the margin component speaks to competitive position, so this is not the definitional identity the critic objected to. It also gives a clean read on which half of the DuPont decomposition the winning interaction actually needs, since the archive has only ever used asset-scaled profitability. Sales and oiadp are among the densest items, so coverage should match the archive norm.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Repeated Debt Service Capacity
evaluated.hypothesis: A firm demonstrates durable financial strength when its annual operating profit has repeatedly been large enough to retire the debt actually falling due, because that history shows it has never needed capital markets to survive its own maturity schedule; the level of profit relative to total claims then refines how much cushion that self-sufficiency carries.
evaluated.reasoning: The counted bar is now operating profit against maturing debt rather than against all current liabilities, which is a threshold a large part of the cross-section clears in some years and fails in others, so the count spreads across its full zero-to-five range instead of collapsing to zero for most firms. The second channel is a smoothed profit-to-total-liabilities coverage level, a quantity not present in the archive, and it supplies continuous variation that breaks the ties inherent in a coarse count, giving stable rather than lumpy portfolio buckets. Neither channel is a previously evaluated signal, so this is a new persistence-plus-cushion construct rather than a splice of two archive entries.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Never Rollover Dependent Profits
evaluated.hypothesis: A single clean year of low short-term debt says little, because firms can temporarily term out debt before reporting; what identifies genuine funding independence is never having leaned on short-dated debt across a full business cycle, so profits earned by a firm whose worst rollover exposure in five years was still low are the most durable.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a worst-case rather than an average operator, so it is not the moving-average smoothing that failed twice in the archive; it asks whether the firm ever entered a state of refinancing dependence, which is the state in which profitable firms are forced into distressed choices. Because the persistence-count construction produced the archive's best Sharpe, there is direct evidence that multi-year conditions on the balance-sheet leg stabilise portfolio composition, and this applies that lesson to the single most reliable quality leg. Ranking keeps the leg bounded, so a handful of crisis-year spikes cannot dominate.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Self Retiring And Habitually Liquid
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, act)), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(SUB(act, lct), 0), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Funding independence has a level dimension and a history dimension: whether liquid assets on hand can retire maturing debt today, and whether the firm has kept its operating cycle self-funded year after year; profitability protected on both dimensions should be the most durable of all.
evaluated.reasoning: The two quality legs being merged were the archive's best on alpha (dlc/act, 3.7%) and on Sharpe (five-year solvency count, 0.332), and they are conceptually near-orthogonal because one is a current stock comparison and the other is a policy track record. Equal-weighting them by SUMRANK before the interaction avoids the double-weighting problem while testing whether level and persistence information are additive, which is the key open question for the consolidation phase. If alpha and Sharpe both exceed the parents, later generations should standardise on this composite quality leg.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Stable Profits Safely Funded
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt)), NEG(VOL(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Earnings stability and funding safety are substitutes in providing durability — a firm can survive volatile profits if it owes nothing soon, and can survive short-dated debt if its profits never move — so the priced quantity is the combination of the two protections rather than either alone.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive's volatility failure (alpha −1.8%) used dollar-denominated EBITDA volatility scaled by current liabilities, which is mechanically a size and growth proxy; scaling the volatility to assets first makes it a genuine profitability-stability measure and demoting it to one of two equally weighted quality channels prevents it from dominating the sort. This is a substantive re-specification of a failed idea rather than a repetition, and it cleanly answers whether earnings stability adds anything once funding structure is controlled. All inputs are dense and the five-year window has cost the archive little coverage.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Peer Relative Margin And Liquidity
evaluated.hypothesis: Operating margins are almost entirely determined by industry technology, so a margin is informative about competitive advantage only relative to direct peers; a firm out-earning its industry on margin while holding enough liquid assets to retire its maturing debt is the clearest case of durable, self-funded operating strength.
evaluated.reasoning: The margin-based signal produced a large alpha but a weak Fama-MacBeth slope and near-zero Sharpe, the classic signature of a pooled sort that is really selecting industries, and industry-neutral ranking is the targeted fix for exactly that pathology rather than a generic wrapper. Pairing it with the self-retirement liquidity leg — also sector-dependent and therefore also industry-ranked — keeps the interaction intact while removing sector bets that FF5 partially absorbs. If the slope rises toward the level of the asset-scaled signals while alpha holds near 4%, the margin channel is salvageable and becomes a strong consolidation candidate.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Profitability Plus Safe Firm Premium
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), MUL(RATIO(oibdp, at), INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt)), -0.1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Profitability is priced everywhere, but an extra premium accrues to profits earned by firms that owe almost nothing within the year, because for those firms the profit stream accrues to shareholders rather than being contingent on creditors renewing their claims; the correct specification therefore keeps the profitability main effect and adds a steeper slope inside the funding-safe group.
evaluated.reasoning: Every archive signal has used a pure rank product, which discards the profitability main effect and equalises the weight of the two legs by construction — a plausible reason the strongest alphas coincide with only moderate Fama-MacBeth slopes; this main-effect-plus-interaction form is a structurally new specification for this archive rather than an average of tested signals. The first channel preserves the full profitability ordering across all firms, while the second adds credit that scales with profitability only where short-term debt is under ten percent of liabilities, so the interaction steepens the profitability slope exactly where the economic story says it should. Inputs are dense, no time window is required, and the threshold is a genuine economic cutoff rather than a fitted parameter.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Hard Claims Versus Soft Claims
evaluated.hypothesis: Holding the total size of the liability stack fixed, financial debt is a hard, contractually enforceable claim that can force liquidation, while payables, accruals and deferred items are soft claims that renew automatically with the business; profitability supported mainly by soft claims is therefore far more durable than identical profitability pledged against hard debt.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a composition measure, not a leverage level: it is invariant to how large total liabilities are relative to assets, so it does not reproduce the profitability-plus-low-leverage quality composite the critic identified, and neither leg reuses the other's numerator so profitability is not double-counted. It also generalises the archive's most reliable finding — that the *type* of claim matters more than its quantity — from the maturity dimension to the enforceability dimension, which is a distinct and untested axis. All four inputs are among the densest annual items, so coverage should sit at the top of the archive range.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Maturity Mismatch Penalty
evaluated.hypothesis: The classic funding pathology is financing illiquid, long-lived assets with debt that matures within a year; profitability generated on a mismatched balance sheet is fragile because the assets cannot be sold to meet the maturities, while the same profitability with maturities matched to liquid assets is safe.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive has compared short-term debt to total liabilities and to current assets, but never to the illiquid asset base it is actually funding, which is the specific comparison that defines maturity mismatch in banking and corporate finance. Because asset-light firms have small illiquid bases, the leg will assign them extreme values, but the rank transform bounds this and the economics are correct: short-dated debt against almost no fixed assets is genuinely precarious. It is a distinct hypothesis from claim composition, and its result will tell us whether the priced quantity is the liability mix or the asset-liability match.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Safely Funded Profit Improvement
evaluated.hypothesis: An increase in operating profitability is credible only when the firm is not simultaneously dependent on short-term creditors, because a rising profit line at a rollover-dependent firm typically reflects cyclical or financing-driven gains that will be reclaimed, while the same improvement at a term-funded firm reflects operating progress the firm can keep.
evaluated.reasoning: The winning architecture has only ever used profitability *levels*, and levels are highly persistent, so the alpha may reflect a static quality tilt rather than the dynamic durability the economic story describes; substituting the one-year change tests whether the funding-safety leg validates news as well as it validates states. This is not a flow signal of the type that has failed — those changed the *quality* leg to a financing flow, whereas here the quality leg keeps its winning level form and only the profitability leg becomes news. A clear result either opens a fresh, lower-correlation direction or definitively confirms the family as a level effect.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Earned Capital Against Total Claims
evaluated.hypothesis: Cumulative retained earnings relative to total obligations measures whether a firm's lifetime profits have already outgrown everything it owes; current profitability at such a firm is the latest instalment of a proven, creditor-independent earning history, whereas identical profitability at a firm whose claims dwarf its accumulated earnings is a first draw on an unproven franchise.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the near-term liquidity and maturity dimensions that the archive has now saturated and substitutes a long-horizon stock measure of solvency: the balance between lifetime earned capital and lifetime claims, which is conceptually orthogonal to whether this year's obligations happen to be short-dated. The two prior retained-earnings attempts scaled re by assets in an additive blend and used its one-year change as a payout proxy; neither compared it with the liability stack inside the multiplicative architecture that actually works in this archive. Both inputs are dense, no window is required, and negative retained earnings rank correctly at the bottom.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Pricing Power With Staying Power
evaluated.hypothesis: A wide margin is only defensible if the firm can afford to wait: holding inventory, extending customer credit and refusing discount demands all require working capital, so high-margin firms with deep liquidity can protect prices through a downturn while equally high-margin but illiquid firms must convert margin into cash by cutting prices.
evaluated.reasoning: The two legs have different denominators — revenue for the profit leg, total liabilities for the buffer leg — so unlike the flagged version this cannot collapse into a single coverage ratio, and it is not a monotone transform of any archived signal. It pairs the leg with the archive's largest alpha (margin, 3.9%) with the leg carrying the archive's best joint record (net working capital over liabilities: fmb 3.20, alpha 4.1%), a pairing never run because margin has only ever been crossed with debt-maturity legs. The economic content is specific: liquidity is what converts pricing power from an accounting fact into a defensible position.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Self Liquidating Profit Premium
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), MUL(RATIO(oibdp, at), INDICATOR(SUB(oibdp, dlc), 0)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Profits carry an extra premium when a single year of operating income would retire every dollar of debt coming due, because such a firm can never be forced to the credit markets by its own maturity schedule; below that line profitability must be discounted for refinancing contingency.
evaluated.reasoning: The gate is now a clean, parameter-free comparison of the profit flow with maturing debt, which eliminates the dlc-inside-lct double counting the critic identified and makes the condition genuinely cross-theme rather than a rescaled version of the gen-4 cutoff. Retaining the profitability main effect in the first channel is the design feature that gave this specification full coverage, a 0.277 Sharpe and a preserved cross-sectional slope, which is exactly the joint-strength profile the objective asks for. Because dlc is small for many firms, the gate splits the cross-section broadly rather than degenerating to a rare condition.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Improving Profits With Deep Buffers
evaluated.hypothesis: A rise in profitability is most likely to stick when the firm holds a deep working-capital buffer, because such a firm can reinvest and hold prices through the ensuing competitive response, whereas a liquidity-constrained firm must monetise the improvement immediately and typically gives it back.
evaluated.reasoning: The profit-change leg has been tested only against debt maturity, and the working-capital buffer leg — the archive's single best on alpha (4.1%) and slope (3.20) — has been tested only against profitability levels, so this pairing is genuinely unexplored and separates whether the change leg needs maturity safety specifically or general balance-sheet slack. It also addresses the persistence critique of level-based signals: if news conditioned on buffers performs at parent level, the family is not merely a static quality tilt. Coverage matches the archive norm with one lag.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Rising Debt Service Coverage
evaluated.hypothesis: What matters for durability is the direction of the firm's solvency position: a profitable firm whose operating profit is growing relative to its total claims — whether by earning more or by retiring obligations — is converting operating success into financial resilience, while flat or deteriorating coverage signals that profits are being absorbed by the balance sheet.
evaluated.reasoning: Every flow construction that failed in this archive applied the change operator to a financing quantity alone (debt growth, payables growth), which is contaminated by investment and size; here the change is applied to the *joint* profit-to-claims ratio, so improvement can come from either side and the measure is scale-free. It is distinct from the profit-change leg because a firm can raise profitability while levering up, which this signal penalises and the pure profit change does not. Inputs are dense and only one lag is required.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Innovation Backed Profits Safely Funded
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Profitability is most persistent when it is defended by continuing investment in the product, and such investment is only sustainable if the firm is not exposed to refinancing pressure that forces discretionary spending cuts; profitable, research-intensive, term-funded firms should therefore have the most durable earning power.
evaluated.reasoning: R&D intensity is the one substantial theme resource the archive has never touched, and it supplies the economic mechanism — a defended competitive position — that the balance-sheet legs cannot express, so it is the batch's genuinely new channel rather than another recombination. Treating unreported R&D as zero is the standard and economically correct convention for firms that genuinely do no research, preserving full coverage instead of restricting the sample to reporters. If the moat channel adds nothing, the final generations can concentrate entirely on funding structure with a clear conscience.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Net Liquid Position After Debt
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, lct), dltt), lt)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The correct measure of financial protection is what remains of a firm's liquid resources once every financial claim, short and long, is deducted: a profitable firm whose current assets exceed both its current liabilities and its funded debt owes its future to no one, while the same profitability with a negative net position is a residual claim behind creditors.
evaluated.reasoning: This fuses into one economic quantity the two legs that have anchored opposite ends of the archive's performance — net working capital over liabilities (best alpha, 4.1%) and financial-debt share of claims (best slope, 3.31) — rather than averaging their ranks, so it tests whether a single net-financial-position measure dominates both parents on the joint criterion. Because liquid resources and funded debt enter with opposite signs in the same numerator, the measure is monotone in exactly the direction the economic story predicts and is scale-free after division by total liabilities. All inputs are dense and no window is required.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Return On Financed Capital With Buffers
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, ADD(ADD(dltt, dlc), ceq))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The economically meaningful profitability rate is the return on capital that actually has to be serviced — funded debt plus shareholders' equity — rather than the return on a total asset base that is partly financed by free operating liabilities; a high return on financed capital held by a firm with deep working-capital buffers is the clearest evidence of a franchise that earns more than its cost of capital and can survive the cycle.
evaluated.reasoning: Every profitability leg in the archive has been scaled by assets or sales, so the invested-capital denominator is a genuinely new normalisation and not an average of tested signals: it mechanically rewards firms that generate profit while employing little financed capital, which is a different ordering from asset-scaled profitability whenever payables and accruals are large. Pairing it with the archive's best-performing quality leg keeps the comparison interpretable, and the two legs share no inputs, so the interaction is not double-counting. All inputs are dense annual items, so coverage should sit at the archive norm.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Working Capital Adjusted Cash Profit
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, DELTA(SUB(act, lct), 1)), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Reported operating profit overstates durable earning power exactly when it is absorbed by a growing investment in receivables and inventory; subtracting the year's increase in net working capital yields the cash the operations actually threw off, and that cash-verified profitability is what determines whether a firm can meet claims without returning to creditors.
evaluated.reasoning: This delivers the cash-verification mechanism the flagged proposal was after while avoiding the coverage collapse the critic correctly identified, because the working-capital change is built from dense balance-sheet items rather than the sparse cash-flow statement item. It is also a sharper test than a cash-coverage safety leg: the adjustment enters the profitability leg itself, so the signal directly contrasts accrual profitability with cash profitability inside the architecture that works. The construction requires one lag and leaves the proven maturity leg untouched, so any change in performance is attributable solely to cash verification of profits.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Expensing Adjusted Profit Safely Funded
evaluated.hypothesis: Accounting expenses research immediately even though it builds a durable asset, so reported operating profit understates the true earning power of research-intensive firms; adding R&D back yields the economically correct profitability measure, and that corrected profitability is most valuable when the firm's funding structure guarantees the research budget will not be cut to meet maturities.
evaluated.reasoning: The breakthrough signal combined profitability and R&D intensity as two averaged ranks, which the critic correctly noted can partly cancel because R&D spending mechanically depresses contemporaneous oibdp; adding R&D back inside a single numerator removes that cancellation and states the hypothesis as a measurement correction rather than a blend of two anomalies. This is the cleanest possible test of whether the gen-6 result is an expensing artefact — the most economically defensible interpretation — and it produces a single profitability variable rather than a composite. Coverage is preserved because non-reporters are correctly treated as spending zero.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Innovation Profits With Deep Buffers
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Research programmes are the first casualty of a liquidity squeeze, so the durability of innovation-backed profitability depends on the firm holding enough working capital to keep spending through a downturn; deep buffers, not merely long-dated debt, are what let a research franchise compound.
evaluated.reasoning: The innovation-augmented profitability leg has only been crossed with the debt-maturity leg, and the archive's two quality legs behave differently — maturity delivers the best t-statistics while working-capital buffers deliver the best raw alpha — so this determines which form of financial health the innovation channel actually requires. It is the single most valuable pairing test available, since the answer directs the final generation's consolidation. Both legs are dense and the construction requires no time window.

evaluated.name: Knowledge Stock Backed Profits
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: What protects a profit stream is the accumulated stock of knowledge capital built over years of sustained research, not the size of this year's research budget, which can spike for one-off reasons; profitability supported by a large knowledge stock and financed with term debt should be the most persistent of all.
evaluated.reasoning: Replacing the current R&D flow with a five-year cumulative spend distinguishes committed, compounding research programmes from firms that happen to be spending heavily this year, which is the difference between a moat and an expense. Scaling the stock by assets rather than sales also breaks the shared-denominator relationship with the margin channel and puts the intangible base on the same footing as the tangible base. The five-year window has historically cost this archive little coverage, and zero-filling remains correct for genuine non-researchers.

evaluated.name: Peer Relative Innovation Intensity
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), IND_ADJ(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale)))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Research intensity is overwhelmingly determined by industry technology, so the informative quantity is how much a firm invests relative to its direct competitors; out-researching peers is what builds relative advantage, whereas a pooled R&D rank mostly identifies pharmaceutical and software membership.
evaluated.reasoning: A 5.1% FF5 alpha from a leg that is strongly sector-clustered raises the concrete risk that the breakthrough is a technology-sector bet that the five factors do not span, and industry-adjusting only the R&D channel isolates that possibility while leaving profitability and funding safety pooled as in the parent. If the alpha survives, the effect is genuinely firm-level and the final consolidation can proceed with confidence; if it collapses, we learn the signal is a sector exposure before committing to it. Industry adjustment also removes the large zero-tied mass problem partially, since non-researchers are demeaned within industries where zero is common.

evaluated.name: Innovation Return On Financed Capital
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(ADD(dltt, dlc), ceq))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The sharpest measure of durable operating strength is the return earned on capital that must actually be serviced, computed after undoing the expensing of research; a firm generating large intangible-adjusted profits on a small base of debt and equity, while holding ample working capital, has both a real economic moat and the means to defend it.
evaluated.reasoning: This combines the two independent improvements discovered in gen 6 — the invested-capital denominator (fmb 3.01, alpha 3.3%) and the R&D adjustment (alpha 5.1%) — into a single profitability variable rather than an average of ranks, so it is a new measurement construct rather than a recombination of signals. Because operating liabilities are excluded from the denominator, the measure is not mechanically related to the working-capital quality leg it is paired with, keeping the interaction clean. All inputs are dense and the expression needs no time window.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Committed Research Programme Profits
evaluated.hypothesis: What distinguishes a genuine technological moat from discretionary spending is continuity: a firm that has run a research programme in every one of the last five years has an institutional commitment that competitors cannot replicate quickly, and profits defended by such a programme are durable provided the firm is not forced by maturing debt to interrupt it.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the SG&A test with a discrimination the archive can actually make — whether the gen-6 breakthrough comes from the *magnitude* of research intensity or from the *continuity* of the research commitment — and a reporting-persistence count cannot mechanically cancel against oibdp the way a spending ratio does, since a count is not an expense netted out of operating income. It is also free of the xsga-subsumes-xrd overlap the critic identified, because the count uses the R&D item directly and measures only its presence across years. Contrasted with the accepted knowledge-stock and intensity variants, the three together decompose the innovation channel into commitment, accumulated stock and current spending, which is exactly the diagnostic the final generation needs.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Intangible Capitalised Return On Assets
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: If research is genuinely an investment, then correcting the accounts requires adding the spending back to profit *and* adding the accumulated knowledge stock to the capital base; the resulting return on total (tangible plus intangible) capital is the economically correct profitability rate, and it is durable precisely when maturing debt cannot force the research programme to be cut.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive has tested the numerator correction (add-back, 4.33/4.9%) and the stock (as a separate ranked channel, 4.69/5.1%) but never the internally consistent capitalisation that puts both corrections in the same ratio, which is the specification implied by the expensing hypothesis and which also removes the double-counting of research-heavy firms that arises when the stock is ranked alongside profitability. Because the denominator grows with the knowledge stock, the measure no longer mechanically favours firms simply for spending, so it separates *productive* research franchises from expensive ones. Coverage is unaffected since non-researchers contribute zero on both sides.

evaluated.name: Research Floor Backed Profits
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 5))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A moat is defended by the research the firm maintains in its worst year, not by its average or cumulative spend: firms that never let research intensity fall below a high floor have made the fixed commitment competitors must match, whereas firms that cut research when conditions tighten reveal that the spending was discretionary.
evaluated.reasoning: The count measures whether research happened and the stock measures how much accumulated, but neither measures the sustained *rate*, and a five-year minimum of research intensity is the sharpest available test of the commitment interpretation that the funding-safety interaction implies. It complements the accepted variants rather than duplicating them, since a firm can score high on cumulative spend while having slashed intensity recently. Zero-filling remains correct: a genuine non-researcher has a floor of zero.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Knowledge Stock And Safe Funding Only
evaluated.hypothesis: If accumulated research capital combined with freedom from refinancing pressure is itself the durable-strength signal, then current accounting profitability adds nothing and may even subtract, because reported profit is depressed by exactly the investment that creates the future franchise.
evaluated.reasoning: This is the attribution experiment the final generation needs: every strong signal in the archive contains a profitability level leg, so we do not know whether that leg still contributes once the knowledge stock is present or whether it is merely along for the ride. A result near the 5.1% parent would show that the innovation-plus-safety pair carries the information and that the last generation should optimise those two legs; a clear drop would confirm that current profitability remains essential and that the composite structure is correct. Inputs are dense and the construction is deliberately minimal.

evaluated.name: Corrected Profit Full Funding Safety
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)), RANK(SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt)), RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Research programmes are threatened both by debt that must be refinanced and by an absence of liquid resources to fund the next development cycle, so the intangible-adjusted profitability of a firm protected on both dimensions should be the most durable of all.
evaluated.reasoning: When innovation profitability was paired with working-capital buffers alone the alpha held at 4.9% but the cross-sectional slope collapsed to 1.60, whereas the maturity leg delivers slopes above 4.3; combining them equally weighted tests whether liquidity adds abnormal return without destroying the slope, which is precisely the joint-evidence trade-off the objective cares about. The profitability leg is the arithmetically clean add-back rather than a rank blend, so any change is attributable solely to the quality composite. Inputs are dense and no window is needed.

evaluated.name: Corrected Profit Against Hard Claims
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: What endangers a research franchise is the presence of enforceable financial claims of any maturity, not merely those due within the year, because long-dated debt still imposes covenants and interest that force discretionary spending cuts in a downturn; the enforceability of claims, rather than their timing, may be the binding constraint.
evaluated.reasoning: The hard-versus-soft-claims leg produced the best cross-sectional slope of any balance-sheet leg (3.31) but only 1.7% alpha when paired with raw profitability, and the natural diagnosis is that the profitability leg was too weak to exploit it; pairing it with the intangible-corrected profit leg is a clean one-change test of whether that diagnosis is right. Together with Signal 5 it completes the quality-leg map for the strongest profit measure — short-dated debt, all financial debt, and debt plus liquidity — which is exactly what the final generation needs to lock in the best combination. Coverage is at the archive maximum.

evaluated.name: Self Financed Knowledge Capital
evaluated.hypothesis: A moat built with owners' money is safer than one built with creditors' money: a firm that has accumulated a large stock of research capital while keeping its total obligations small has financed its competitive position from internal profits, so no creditor can force it to abandon that position, whereas an equally research-heavy firm with a large claim stack has effectively pledged its moat.
evaluated.reasoning: Rather than stacking two tested R&D proxies on the profitability side, this puts research capital and total claims into a single scale-free quantity on the quality side, so the interaction being tested is the *financing source* of the intangible base rather than the timing of the debt that happens to sit against it. It is distinct from the archived knowledge-stock signal, which scaled the stock by assets and conditioned separately on short-term debt: here a firm with a large research base and heavy long-term obligations is penalised, which the parent does not do. Inputs are dense, the zero-fill convention remains economically correct for non-researchers, and the five-year window has cost this archive no coverage.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Conjunctive Profit Knowledge Safety
evaluated.expression: MUL(MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Durable operating strength requires all three attributes at once — the firm must actually earn profits today, own an accumulated research base that defends them tomorrow, and owe nothing soon that could force it to liquidate either; a firm missing any one of the three should not sit in the long leg.
evaluated.reasoning: Every innovation signal in the archive averages profitability and research inside a SUMRANK, which lets an extreme R&D rank carry unprofitable firms into the top bucket — the precise mechanism that produced a 5.7% alpha with a 1.45 slope when profitability was removed entirely. Replacing the additive blend with a conjunction forces the long leg to satisfy the profitability condition as well, which should restore the strong Fama-MacBeth slope while retaining the research-driven abnormal return. This is an economically motivated change of the conjunction logic rather than a new ingredient, and coverage is unchanged at the archive maximum.

evaluated.name: Corrected Profit Self Financed Moat
evaluated.hypothesis: A moat financed by owners rather than creditors is the durable kind: a firm with high intangible-adjusted profitability that has accumulated its research base while keeping total claims small owns its competitive position outright, so neither the profits nor the research programme is contingent on credit conditions.
evaluated.reasoning: This unites the archive's two highest-Sharpe elements — the expensing-corrected profit leg (0.302) and claim-scaled knowledge capital (0.369, slope 4.08) — with a single controlled change from Self Financed Knowledge Capital, namely correcting the profitability numerator that R&D spending mechanically depresses. Because the quality leg scales research capital by total liabilities rather than assets, the interaction penalises heavily indebted researchers, which the maturity-based signals do not, giving a distinct portfolio composition and the best chance of high risk-adjusted return. Inputs are dense and no additional window is introduced.

evaluated.name: Innovation Bonus For Safe Firms
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), MUL(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at), INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt)), -0.1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Profitability is priced across the whole cross-section, but investors additionally underprice the accumulated research base of firms that are free of refinancing pressure, because only those firms can be confident of carrying the programme to commercial fruition; research capital at rollover-dependent firms deserves no such premium.
evaluated.reasoning: Every innovation signal so far is a pure rank product, which discards the profitability main effect and therefore trades slope against alpha; this specification keeps the full profitability ordering in the first channel and adds a knowledge-stock credit only inside the funding-safe group, which is structurally different from anything in the innovation family and is the design that historically produced the archive's most stable portfolios (Sharpe 0.277–0.309 with full coverage). Because the interaction term is exactly zero for rollover-dependent firms, the signal implements the conditional-premium hypothesis literally rather than through a smooth product. Inputs are dense and the threshold is an economic cutoff on short-term debt share, not a fitted parameter.

evaluated.name: Short Debt Against Illiquid Capital
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, ADD(SUB(at, act), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Knowledge capital is the least saleable asset a firm owns, so a research-intensive company that funds itself with debt maturing inside a year is running the most acute form of asset-liability mismatch: the assets backing the debt cannot be liquidated at all, and a refinancing failure destroys the franchise rather than merely shrinking it.
evaluated.reasoning: The flagged version was numerically dominated by current assets and therefore collapsed onto the already-tested working-capital leg; this instead scales short-term debt by the illiquid asset base, tangible plus intangible, so the leg is a genuine mismatch measure and rises only when maturing debt is large relative to assets that cannot be sold. It extends the gen-5 maturity-mismatch construct (3.0% alpha with raw profitability) by recognising that for research firms the illiquid base includes accumulated R&D, which is exactly the interaction the innovation family implies but has never tested. Coverage is unaffected since all inputs are dense and the zero-fill convention is unchanged.

evaluated.name: Franchise Strength Three Channels
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), SUMRANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at), RATIO(oiadp, sale)))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A durable franchise rests on three separable pillars — capital productivity, an accumulated knowledge base, and pricing power in the product market — and only a firm strong on all three, and free of refinancing pressure, has operating strength that competitors cannot erode.
evaluated.reasoning: The critic is right that the R&D stock and the R&D floor are monotone in the same underlying intensity, so the third channel here is operating margin, which is economically and statistically distinct: it delivered 3.9% alpha with a 1.22 slope in isolation, the mirror image of the asset-scaled profitability leg's profile, indicating low overlap rather than redundancy. Adding pricing power rather than a second research statistic gives the composite genuine breadth while keeping the profitability side dominant at two of three channels, which protects the cross-sectional slope. All inputs are dense and no new window is introduced.

evaluated.name: Peer Profitability Knowledge Safety
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Asset-scaled profitability is largely determined by industry capital intensity, so the informative quantity is how profitable a firm is relative to its direct competitors; measuring the profit channel peer-relative while leaving the research and funding channels pooled should identify firms that are genuinely out-earning rivals behind a defended, safely financed position.

Because sector effects in profit margins are exactly what dilute a pooled profit rank, this targets the slope side of the joint objective while leaving the alpha-generating research and maturity legs untouched. Coverage is unchanged at the archive maximum and no additional data items are required.

considered.name: Improving Profits With Earned Capital
considered.hypothesis: An upward trend in operating profitability is credible when the firm has a deep stock of retained earnings, since cumulative internally generated capital verifies that past profits were real and reinvestable rather than one-time or externally financed.
considered.reasoning: TREND captures the profitability-improvement channel while retained earnings over assets is a balance-sheet quality/maturity measure of accumulated earnings history, so the pair distinguishes a genuine profitability ramp from a fragile turnaround at a capital-depleted firm. Neither leg alone contains this validation logic: young cash-burning firms can trend upward from a very low base, and mature high-RE firms can be stagnant. The rank combination keeps both channels on a comparable scale and preserves broad coverage.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Interest Adjusted Profit With Debt Coverage
considered.hypothesis: Profitability net of the cost of debt, combined with the ability of operating cash flow to service total liabilities, isolates operating strength that belongs to shareholders rather than profitability that is manufactured or claimed by leverage.
considered.reasoning: The first rank is a profitability spread after financing costs (profitability theme adjusted for the capital structure claim) and the second is a cash-flow-to-liabilities solvency ratio (quality theme), so the product is high only when profits survive interest and cash flow comfortably covers obligations. This penalizes the classic levered-ROE illusion, where high equity returns simply reflect debt amplification. It should produce a long leg of unlevered, cash-generative compounders and a short leg of levered, cash-poor firms.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Trough Tested Operating Profitability
considered.hypothesis: Current operating profitability is durable only if the firm stayed solidly profitable in its worst year of the last five; a high profit floor, not symmetric earnings dispersion, is what distinguishes a protected franchise from a cyclical windfall.
considered.reasoning: Replacing the volatility denominator with a downside floor removes the mechanical fragility of dividing a signed mean by a near-zero standard deviation, and both legs are mapped into bounded cross-sectional ranks so loss-making and profitable firms are scored on one comparable scale. The interaction is genuine: the same current EBITDA/assets is up-weighted only when the five-year minimum net-income-to-assets is also high, so cyclical peakers and firms with a recent loss year are pushed out of the long leg. This is a downside-persistence concept rather than the standard earnings-volatility anomaly, and it needs no outlier winsorization to behave.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Worst Of Accrual And Cash Profitability
considered.hypothesis: A firm is only genuinely profitable if it looks profitable on both the accrual and the cash measure relative to its industry; the binding weaker of the two measures is the honest estimate of operating strength, and the market anchors instead on the more flattering one.
considered.reasoning: The MIN operator is a strictly non-additive conditioning device: a high score is impossible unless accrual profitability and cash profitability are simultaneously strong, so the signal cannot be reproduced by any weighted sum of Novy-Marx profitability and Sloan accruals. Industry adjustment puts the two channels on a common, capital-intensity-neutral footing so the minimum is economically meaningful rather than driven by depreciation or working-capital conventions. Firms whose reported profits outrun cash generation are automatically scored by their cash number, and vice versa, which is exactly the durable-versus-manufactured distinction.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Liquidity Reinforced Gross Profitability
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), MUL(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), INDICATOR(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt), 0)))
considered.hypothesis: Gross profitability is priced too weakly when the firm can self-fund its operating cycle; solvency should amplify the profitability signal rather than define the short leg, since illiquid firms with weak margins, not illiquid firms per se, are the losers.
considered.reasoning: The first channel preserves the full cross-sectional ordering of gross profitability for every firm, so no company is forced to the bottom purely for failing a working-capital test; the second channel gives extra credit that scales with profitability but only accrues to firms with positive net working capital relative to total liabilities. The result is a graded interaction in which the healthy-firm profitability slope is steeper than the fragile-firm slope, which is what the hypothesis actually claims. The short leg is therefore populated by low-margin firms regardless of liquidity, avoiding a pure distress portfolio.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Rank Space Persistent Profitability
considered.hypothesis: Investors price the current level of profitability but underweight the track record behind it, so firms that are both highly profitable now and profitable in every one of the last five years earn abnormal returns relative to equally profitable firms with a broken history.
considered.reasoning: Ranking the smoothed operating ROA before multiplying removes the zero-crossing pathology of the original form: chronic loss-makers now score near the bottom on both bounded rank channels instead of collapsing to exactly zero and jumping above mildly unprofitable firms. Monotonicity in each argument is preserved, and the product still requires both high current profitability and a full history of positive earnings to reach the top decile. The persistence count is coarse and outlier-immune, so it complements rather than duplicates level-based profitability measures.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Profits Not Propped By New Debt
considered.hypothesis: Sustained operating profitability accompanied by shrinking or flat debt reflects genuine internal cash generation, while equally high reported profitability alongside rapid new borrowing signals profits being financed and flattered by balance-sheet expansion that will reverse.
considered.reasoning: This is a flow rather than a level mechanism: it conditions the profitability state on the direction of debt financing over the past year, so it separates self-funding operators from firms whose apparent strength coincides with creditor support. The three-year moving average removes single-year profit noise without imposing the coverage cost of a five-year window. It tests a financing-flow channel that neither gen-0 survivor examined.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Working Capital Backed Profitability
considered.hypothesis: High operating profitability is more likely to persist when the firm holds enough net working capital relative to its total obligations to fund the operating cycle internally, since liquidity-constrained profitable firms must divert operating cash to near-term claims rather than to shareholders.
considered.reasoning: This is the graded repair of the gen-0 binary solvency gate: net working capital scaled by total liabilities enters as a continuous rank, so firms are ordered smoothly by liquidity instead of being dumped en masse into the short leg, which prevents the spread from degenerating into a pure distress bet. Both legs use high-coverage annual items and no time window at all, so it should have the broadest coverage in this batch. It isolates the liquidity channel of financial health, separate from the debt-level channel in Signal 1.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Total Leverage Discounted Profitability
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), RANK(NEG(MUL(RATIO(xsga, sale), RATIO(lt, at)))))
considered.hypothesis: Profitability is fragile when the firm carries both high fixed operating costs and high financial obligations, because the combined operating-and-financial leverage converts modest revenue shortfalls into large earnings declines; the same profitability at a low-total-leverage firm is far more likely to persist.
considered.reasoning: The penalty term multiplies an operating-rigidity proxy (SG&A intensity of sales, a profitability-theme item) by a solvency proxy (total liabilities over assets, a quality-theme item), so it captures the compounding of the two leverages rather than either one in isolation. This is a genuinely different mechanism from simple debt-level conditioning: it predicts that fixed-cost-heavy firms need clean balance sheets for their profits to be durable. Both inputs are broadly reported, and the rank product keeps the signal bounded and monotone in each leg.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Rollover Risk Adjusted Profitability
considered.hypothesis: What makes profitability fragile is not the amount of debt but its maturity: a profitable firm whose claims are concentrated in debt due within a year must keep refinancing at the mercy of credit markets, so its operating strength is hostage to rollover conditions, while the same profitability financed with long-dated or non-debt claims is insulated.
considered.reasoning: The quality leg is the short-term share of the liability structure, which is orthogonal by construction to the leverage level used in Quality-Minus-Junk safety, so this tests maturity composition rather than rediscovering profitability-plus-low-leverage. The interaction is the point: refinancing risk should erode the value of high operating profitability far more than it matters for firms with little profit to protect, and the rank product concentrates the long leg on profitable firms with term-funded balance sheets. Scaling short-term debt by total liabilities rather than assets keeps the measure defined for debt-free firms and avoids simply re-expressing total leverage.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Distribution Verified Profitability
considered.hypothesis: Reported profits are credible when the firm actually hands cash to shareholders; using the retained-earnings identity, income not added to retained earnings is the payout, so profitability accompanied by real distributions reflects durable earning power rather than accounting income that can only ever be reinvested or written off.

Both inputs are widely reported and only a one-year lag is required, so coverage should remain high.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Stable Financing Durable Profits
considered.hypothesis: A firm with genuinely durable operating strength does not have to keep re-levering and de-levering to fund itself, so an erratic liability-to-assets path reveals funding dependence and earnings fragility even when the current profitability level looks strong.
considered.reasoning: Replacing the F-score's Δleverage and Δliquidity indicators with the *volatility* of the capital-structure path changes the economic object from a one-year directional improvement to the stability of the financing model, which is not a published score component and cannot be captured by any single-year change. The multiplicative rank form gives each leg equal weight, fixing the silent double-weighting of the nested SUMRANK, and the four-year volatility window is short enough to preserve reasonable coverage. The prediction is a joint one: financing stability should be rewarded mainly where there are substantial profits to sustain.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Profit Coverage Of Near Term Claims
considered.hypothesis: The relevant measure of durable operating strength is how many times current-year operating profit covers the claims coming due within the year; a firm whose annual EBITDA dwarfs its current liabilities is structurally insulated, while an equally profitable firm whose near-term claims exceed its profit stream is one bad year from creditor control.

Industry adjustment is essential because current-liability intensity is highly sector-dependent (retail and utilities versus software), so the raw ratio would otherwise sort industries rather than firms. Both inputs are among the best-populated annual items, so coverage should be at the high end of the archive.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Funding Pressure Adjusted Profitability
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt), NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt)))))
considered.hypothesis: Liquidity buffers and debt-maturity structure are two separable dimensions of near-term funding pressure, and profitability is most durable when both are favourable: liquid resources cover the operating cycle *and* little of the liability stack must be refinanced immediately.

The inner SUMRANK equalises the weight of the liquidity and maturity legs before they gate profitability, avoiding the silent double-weighting problem flagged earlier. Coverage should match the parents since all four inputs are standard balance-sheet items.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Profits Without Payables Stretch
considered.hypothesis: A profitable firm that is quietly financing itself by letting current liabilities outrun its sales base is converting supplier and accrual credit into reported operating strength; that funding source is finite and reversible, so such profitability is less durable than profitability generated with a stable trade-credit position.

Benchmarking current-liability growth against contemporaneous sales growth removes the mechanical scaling that made the raw debt-growth leg behave like a size-and-investment tilt. It gives the batch one genuine flow mechanism to sit alongside the level-based consolidation, so we learn whether *any* flow variable can work in this theme pair or whether only levels do.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Habitually Liquid Profitable Firms
considered.hypothesis: A liquidity buffer is a policy, not an accident: firms that have maintained positive net working capital in every one of the last five years have demonstrated an institutionalised commitment to self-funding their operating cycle, and their current profitability is therefore far more likely to survive a demand or credit shock than the profitability of a firm that only happens to be liquid this year.

The count is coarse and outlier-immune, so unlike the level-based liquidity leg it cannot be driven by a handful of cash-hoarding observations, and ranking it before multiplication keeps both legs bounded with no zero-crossing pathology. It also tells us something decision-relevant: whether the archive's liquidity payoff comes from the current buffer size or from a persistent financial policy.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Implied Borrowing Rate Discount
considered.hypothesis: The rate lenders actually charge is an informed external verdict on earnings durability, so among borrowers, high operating profitability obtained at a low effective interest rate reflects credit-market confirmation of the franchise, while the same profitability funded at a punitive rate signals that specialists with access to private information regard the profits as fragile.

Winsorising the ratio controls the small-denominator explosions that arise for firms with trivial debt balances, and firms with no debt simply drop out, which is economically correct because there is no lender verdict to observe. Coverage will be the key diagnostic on whether creditor-priced information can be used at all in this theme pair.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Trough Profit Cover Of Current Claims
considered.hypothesis: Financial durability should be assessed under stress: the right question is not whether this year's profit covers claims coming due, but whether the firm's *worst* operating profit of the recent past would still have covered them, since that is the state in which creditors force asset sales or dilutive financing.

Industry adjustment is necessary because both the cyclicality of EBITDA and the intensity of current liabilities are sector traits, so the raw ratio would sort industries rather than firms. Using a minimum rather than a mean or standard deviation keeps the emphasis on downside survivability, which is the part of stability that creditors and equity holders actually care about.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Rollover Need Versus Liquid Resources
considered.hypothesis: Refinancing risk is not about how much of the liability stack is short-dated but about whether liquid resources already on hand can retire the maturing debt; a profitable firm whose current assets far exceed its short-term debt faces no rollover decision at all, whereas one with the same maturity mix but thin liquid assets must return to lenders on their terms.

Both inputs are dense, so coverage should be at the top of the archive range.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Within Industry Profit And Maturity
considered.hypothesis: Both operating profitability and reliance on short-term debt are heavily sector-determined, so the priced information should be a firm's standing relative to its industry peers rather than its position in the pooled cross-section; industry-neutral scoring should raise abnormal returns by stripping out sector bets that FF5 factors partly absorb.

considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Profit Volatility Against Obligations
considered.hypothesis: Fragility arises when the variability of the profit stream is large relative to the obligations that must be paid regardless of business conditions; a firm whose EBITDA fluctuates by a small fraction of its current liabilities can always service them, while equal profitability with fluctuations comparable to its near-term claims implies a real probability of a funding shortfall.
