The five-year window is affordable given that comparable windows have cost the archive little coverage.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Rising Short Debt Reliance Penalty
considered.hypothesis: A profitable firm that is actively shifting its funding toward short-dated debt is revealing either loss of access to term credit or a deliberate bet on refinancing conditions, and that migration predicts deterioration in the durability of its profits even before the level of short-term debt looks alarming.

The construction is bounded, uses only dense items, and requires a single lag.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Pricing Power With Term Funding
considered.hypothesis: Durable operating strength shows up as pricing power — profit per dollar of revenue after depreciation — rather than as profit per dollar of assets, and pricing power is only bankable for equity holders when the firm is not forced to renegotiate its funding each year; margin-strong firms with term-funded balance sheets can defend prices through downturns instead of discounting to raise cash.

Sales and oiadp are among the densest items, so coverage should match the archive norm.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Repeated Debt Service Capacity
considered.hypothesis: A firm demonstrates durable financial strength when its annual operating profit has repeatedly been large enough to retire the debt actually falling due, because that history shows it has never needed capital markets to survive its own maturity schedule; the level of profit relative to total claims then refines how much cushion that self-sufficiency carries.

considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Never Rollover Dependent Profits
considered.hypothesis: A single clean year of low short-term debt says little, because firms can temporarily term out debt before reporting; what identifies genuine funding independence is never having leaned on short-dated debt across a full business cycle, so profits earned by a firm whose worst rollover exposure in five years was still low are the most durable.

Because the persistence-count construction produced the archive's best Sharpe, there is direct evidence that multi-year conditions on the balance-sheet leg stabilise portfolio composition, and this applies that lesson to the single most reliable quality leg. Ranking keeps the leg bounded, so a handful of crisis-year spikes cannot dominate.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Self Retiring And Habitually Liquid
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, act)), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(SUB(act, lct), 0), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Funding independence has a level dimension and a history dimension: whether liquid assets on hand can retire maturing debt today, and whether the firm has kept its operating cycle self-funded year after year; profitability protected on both dimensions should be the most durable of all.

Equal-weighting them by SUMRANK before the interaction avoids the double-weighting problem while testing whether level and persistence information are additive, which is the key open question for the consolidation phase. If alpha and Sharpe both exceed the parents, later generations should standardise on this composite quality leg.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Stable Profits Safely Funded
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt)), NEG(VOL(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: Earnings stability and funding safety are substitutes in providing durability — a firm can survive volatile profits if it owes nothing soon, and can survive short-dated debt if its profits never move — so the priced quantity is the combination of the two protections rather than either alone.

This is a substantive re-specification of a failed idea rather than a repetition, and it cleanly answers whether earnings stability adds anything once funding structure is controlled. All inputs are dense and the five-year window has cost the archive little coverage.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Peer Relative Margin And Liquidity
considered.hypothesis: Operating margins are almost entirely determined by industry technology, so a margin is informative about competitive advantage only relative to direct peers; a firm out-earning its industry on margin while holding enough liquid assets to retire its maturing debt is the clearest case of durable, self-funded operating strength.
considered.reasoning: The margin-based signal produced a large alpha but a weak Fama-MacBeth slope and near-zero Sharpe, the classic signature of a pooled sort that is really selecting industries, and industry-neutral ranking is the targeted fix for exactly that pathology rather than a generic wrapper. Pairing it with the self-retirement liquidity leg — also sector-dependent and therefore also industry-ranked — keeps the interaction intact while removing sector bets that FF5 partially absorbs. If the slope rises toward the level of the asset-scaled signals while alpha holds near 4%, the margin channel is salvageable and becomes a strong consolidation candidate.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Profitability Plus Safe Firm Premium
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), MUL(RATIO(oibdp, at), INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt)), -0.1)))
considered.hypothesis: Profitability is priced everywhere, but an extra premium accrues to profits earned by firms that owe almost nothing within the year, because for those firms the profit stream accrues to shareholders rather than being contingent on creditors renewing their claims; the correct specification therefore keeps the profitability main effect and adds a steeper slope inside the funding-safe group.

The first channel preserves the full profitability ordering across all firms, while the second adds credit that scales with profitability only where short-term debt is under ten percent of liabilities, so the interaction steepens the profitability slope exactly where the economic story says it should. Inputs are dense, no time window is required, and the threshold is a genuine economic cutoff rather than a fitted parameter.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Hard Claims Versus Soft Claims
considered.hypothesis: Holding the total size of the liability stack fixed, financial debt is a hard, contractually enforceable claim that can force liquidation, while payables, accruals and deferred items are soft claims that renew automatically with the business; profitability supported mainly by soft claims is therefore far more durable than identical profitability pledged against hard debt.
considered.reasoning: This is a composition measure, not a leverage level: it is invariant to how large total liabilities are relative to assets, so it does not reproduce the profitability-plus-low-leverage quality composite the critic identified, and neither leg reuses the other's numerator so profitability is not double-counted. It also generalises the archive's most reliable finding — that the *type* of claim matters more than its quantity — from the maturity dimension to the enforceability dimension, which is a distinct and untested axis. All four inputs are among the densest annual items, so coverage should sit at the top of the archive range.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Cash Profitability With Term Funding
considered.hypothesis: Operating cash flow is the profitability measure that cannot be manufactured by accrual choices, and it is precisely the measure that determines whether maturing obligations can actually be met; cash-generative firms with little short-dated debt therefore represent the strongest form of durable operating strength.
considered.reasoning: The archive has run accrual-based EBITDA, after-depreciation operating income and margins through the winning architecture but has never run operating cash flow through it, even though the entire economic story is about profits that convert into the resources needed to service claims. This tests whether the interaction strengthens when the profitability leg is cash-verified, which would be the single most economically meaningful upgrade available to the family. The coverage statistic is the key risk and the key diagnostic, since the only prior oancf signal also carried the sparse xint item and reported 0.08 coverage.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Maturity Mismatch Penalty
considered.hypothesis: The classic funding pathology is financing illiquid, long-lived assets with debt that matures within a year; profitability generated on a mismatched balance sheet is fragile because the assets cannot be sold to meet the maturities, while the same profitability with maturities matched to liquid assets is safe.
considered.reasoning: The archive has compared short-term debt to total liabilities and to current assets, but never to the illiquid asset base it is actually funding, which is the specific comparison that defines maturity mismatch in banking and corporate finance. Because asset-light firms have small illiquid bases, the leg will assign them extreme values, but the rank transform bounds this and the economics are correct: short-dated debt against almost no fixed assets is genuinely precarious. It is a distinct hypothesis from claim composition, and its result will tell us whether the priced quantity is the liability mix or the asset-liability match.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Safely Funded Profit Improvement
considered.hypothesis: An increase in operating profitability is credible only when the firm is not simultaneously dependent on short-term creditors, because a rising profit line at a rollover-dependent firm typically reflects cyclical or financing-driven gains that will be reclaimed, while the same improvement at a term-funded firm reflects operating progress the firm can keep.
considered.reasoning: The winning architecture has only ever used profitability *levels*, and levels are highly persistent, so the alpha may reflect a static quality tilt rather than the dynamic durability the economic story describes; substituting the one-year change tests whether the funding-safety leg validates news as well as it validates states. This is not a flow signal of the type that has failed — those changed the *quality* leg to a financing flow, whereas here the quality leg keeps its winning level form and only the profitability leg becomes news. A clear result either opens a fresh, lower-correlation direction or definitively confirms the family as a level effect.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Earned Capital Against Total Claims
considered.hypothesis: Cumulative retained earnings relative to total obligations measures whether a firm's lifetime profits have already outgrown everything it owes; current profitability at such a firm is the latest instalment of a proven, creditor-independent earning history, whereas identical profitability at a firm whose claims dwarf its accumulated earnings is a first draw on an unproven franchise.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the near-term liquidity and maturity dimensions that the archive has now saturated and substitutes a long-horizon stock measure of solvency: the balance between lifetime earned capital and lifetime claims, which is conceptually orthogonal to whether this year's obligations happen to be short-dated. The two prior retained-earnings attempts scaled re by assets in an additive blend and used its one-year change as a payout proxy; neither compared it with the liability stack inside the multiplicative architecture that actually works in this archive. Both inputs are dense, no window is required, and negative retained earnings rank correctly at the bottom.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Pricing Power With Staying Power
considered.hypothesis: A wide margin is only defensible if the firm can afford to wait: holding inventory, extending customer credit and refusing discount demands all require working capital, so high-margin firms with deep liquidity can protect prices through a downturn while equally high-margin but illiquid firms must convert margin into cash by cutting prices.
considered.reasoning: The two legs have different denominators — revenue for the profit leg, total liabilities for the buffer leg — so unlike the flagged version this cannot collapse into a single coverage ratio, and it is not a monotone transform of any archived signal. It pairs the leg with the archive's largest alpha (margin, 3.9%) with the leg carrying the archive's best joint record (net working capital over liabilities: fmb 3.20, alpha 4.1%), a pairing never run because margin has only ever been crossed with debt-maturity legs. The economic content is specific: liquidity is what converts pricing power from an accounting fact into a defensible position.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Self Liquidating Profit Premium
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), MUL(RATIO(oibdp, at), INDICATOR(SUB(oibdp, dlc), 0)))
considered.hypothesis: Profits carry an extra premium when a single year of operating income would retire every dollar of debt coming due, because such a firm can never be forced to the credit markets by its own maturity schedule; below that line profitability must be discounted for refinancing contingency.
considered.reasoning: The gate is now a clean, parameter-free comparison of the profit flow with maturing debt, which eliminates the dlc-inside-lct double counting the critic identified and makes the condition genuinely cross-theme rather than a rescaled version of the gen-4 cutoff. Retaining the profitability main effect in the first channel is the design feature that gave this specification full coverage, a 0.277 Sharpe and a preserved cross-sectional slope, which is exactly the joint-strength profile the objective asks for. Because dlc is small for many firms, the gate splits the cross-section broadly rather than degenerating to a rare condition.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Improving Profits With Deep Buffers
considered.hypothesis: A rise in profitability is most likely to stick when the firm holds a deep working-capital buffer, because such a firm can reinvest and hold prices through the ensuing competitive response, whereas a liquidity-constrained firm must monetise the improvement immediately and typically gives it back.
considered.reasoning: The profit-change leg has been tested only against debt maturity, and the working-capital buffer leg — the archive's single best on alpha (4.1%) and slope (3.20) — has been tested only against profitability levels, so this pairing is genuinely unexplored and separates whether the change leg needs maturity safety specifically or general balance-sheet slack. It also addresses the persistence critique of level-based signals: if news conditioned on buffers performs at parent level, the family is not merely a static quality tilt. Coverage matches the archive norm with one lag.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Rising Debt Service Coverage
considered.hypothesis: What matters for durability is the direction of the firm's solvency position: a profitable firm whose operating profit is growing relative to its total claims — whether by earning more or by retiring obligations — is converting operating success into financial resilience, while flat or deteriorating coverage signals that profits are being absorbed by the balance sheet.
considered.reasoning: Every flow construction that failed in this archive applied the change operator to a financing quantity alone (debt growth, payables growth), which is contaminated by investment and size; here the change is applied to the *joint* profit-to-claims ratio, so improvement can come from either side and the measure is scale-free. It is distinct from the profit-change leg because a firm can raise profitability while levering up, which this signal penalises and the pure profit change does not. Inputs are dense and only one lag is required.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Innovation Backed Profits Safely Funded
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Profitability is most persistent when it is defended by continuing investment in the product, and such investment is only sustainable if the firm is not exposed to refinancing pressure that forces discretionary spending cuts; profitable, research-intensive, term-funded firms should therefore have the most durable earning power.
considered.reasoning: R&D intensity is the one substantial theme resource the archive has never touched, and it supplies the economic mechanism — a defended competitive position — that the balance-sheet legs cannot express, so it is the batch's genuinely new channel rather than another recombination. Treating unreported R&D as zero is the standard and economically correct convention for firms that genuinely do no research, preserving full coverage instead of restricting the sample to reporters. If the moat channel adds nothing, the final generations can concentrate entirely on funding structure with a clear conscience.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Net Liquid Position After Debt
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, lct), dltt), lt)))
considered.hypothesis: The correct measure of financial protection is what remains of a firm's liquid resources once every financial claim, short and long, is deducted: a profitable firm whose current assets exceed both its current liabilities and its funded debt owes its future to no one, while the same profitability with a negative net position is a residual claim behind creditors.
considered.reasoning: This fuses into one economic quantity the two legs that have anchored opposite ends of the archive's performance — net working capital over liabilities (best alpha, 4.1%) and financial-debt share of claims (best slope, 3.31) — rather than averaging their ranks, so it tests whether a single net-financial-position measure dominates both parents on the joint criterion. Because liquid resources and funded debt enter with opposite signs in the same numerator, the measure is monotone in exactly the direction the economic story predicts and is scale-free after division by total liabilities. All inputs are dense and no window is required.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Return On Financed Capital With Buffers
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, ADD(ADD(dltt, dlc), ceq))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))
considered.hypothesis: The economically meaningful profitability rate is the return on capital that actually has to be serviced — funded debt plus shareholders' equity — rather than the return on a total asset base that is partly financed by free operating liabilities; a high return on financed capital held by a firm with deep working-capital buffers is the clearest evidence of a franchise that earns more than its cost of capital and can survive the cycle.
considered.reasoning: Every profitability leg in the archive has been scaled by assets or sales, so the invested-capital denominator is a genuinely new normalisation and not an average of tested signals: it mechanically rewards firms that generate profit while employing little financed capital, which is a different ordering from asset-scaled profitability whenever payables and accruals are large. Pairing it with the archive's best-performing quality leg keeps the comparison interpretable, and the two legs share no inputs, so the interaction is not double-counting. All inputs are dense annual items, so coverage should sit at the archive norm.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Working Capital Adjusted Cash Profit
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, DELTA(SUB(act, lct), 1)), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Reported operating profit overstates durable earning power exactly when it is absorbed by a growing investment in receivables and inventory; subtracting the year's increase in net working capital yields the cash the operations actually threw off, and that cash-verified profitability is what determines whether a firm can meet claims without returning to creditors.
considered.reasoning: This delivers the cash-verification mechanism the flagged proposal was after while avoiding the coverage collapse the critic correctly identified, because the working-capital change is built from dense balance-sheet items rather than the sparse cash-flow statement item. It is also a sharper test than a cash-coverage safety leg: the adjustment enters the profitability leg itself, so the signal directly contrasts accrual profitability with cash profitability inside the architecture that works. The construction requires one lag and leaves the proven maturity leg untouched, so any change in performance is attributable solely to cash verification of profits.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Expensing Adjusted Profit Safely Funded
considered.hypothesis: Accounting expenses research immediately even though it builds a durable asset, so reported operating profit understates the true earning power of research-intensive firms; adding R&D back yields the economically correct profitability measure, and that corrected profitability is most valuable when the firm's funding structure guarantees the research budget will not be cut to meet maturities.
considered.reasoning: The breakthrough signal combined profitability and R&D intensity as two averaged ranks, which the critic correctly noted can partly cancel because R&D spending mechanically depresses contemporaneous oibdp; adding R&D back inside a single numerator removes that cancellation and states the hypothesis as a measurement correction rather than a blend of two anomalies. This is the cleanest possible test of whether the gen-6 result is an expensing artefact — the most economically defensible interpretation — and it produces a single profitability variable rather than a composite. Coverage is preserved because non-reporters are correctly treated as spending zero.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Innovation Profits With Deep Buffers
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))
considered.hypothesis: Research programmes are the first casualty of a liquidity squeeze, so the durability of innovation-backed profitability depends on the firm holding enough working capital to keep spending through a downturn; deep buffers, not merely long-dated debt, are what let a research franchise compound.
considered.reasoning: The innovation-augmented profitability leg has only been crossed with the debt-maturity leg, and the archive's two quality legs behave differently — maturity delivers the best t-statistics while working-capital buffers deliver the best raw alpha — so this determines which form of financial health the innovation channel actually requires. It is the single most valuable pairing test available, since the answer directs the final generation's consolidation. Both legs are dense and the construction requires no time window.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Knowledge Stock Backed Profits
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: What protects a profit stream is the accumulated stock of knowledge capital built over years of sustained research, not the size of this year's research budget, which can spike for one-off reasons; profitability supported by a large knowledge stock and financed with term debt should be the most persistent of all.
considered.reasoning: Replacing the current R&D flow with a five-year cumulative spend distinguishes committed, compounding research programmes from firms that happen to be spending heavily this year, which is the difference between a moat and an expense. Scaling the stock by assets rather than sales also breaks the shared-denominator relationship with the margin channel and puts the intangible base on the same footing as the tangible base. The five-year window has historically cost this archive little coverage, and zero-filling remains correct for genuine non-researchers.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Peer Relative Innovation Intensity
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), IND_ADJ(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale)))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Research intensity is overwhelmingly determined by industry technology, so the informative quantity is how much a firm invests relative to its direct competitors; out-researching peers is what builds relative advantage, whereas a pooled R&D rank mostly identifies pharmaceutical and software membership.
considered.reasoning: A 5.1% FF5 alpha from a leg that is strongly sector-clustered raises the concrete risk that the breakthrough is a technology-sector bet that the five factors do not span, and industry-adjusting only the R&D channel isolates that possibility while leaving profitability and funding safety pooled as in the parent. If the alpha survives, the effect is genuinely firm-level and the final consolidation can proceed with confidence; if it collapses, we learn the signal is a sector exposure before committing to it. Industry adjustment also removes the large zero-tied mass problem partially, since non-researchers are demeaned within industries where zero is common.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Innovation Return On Financed Capital
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(ADD(dltt, dlc), ceq))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))
considered.hypothesis: The sharpest measure of durable operating strength is the return earned on capital that must actually be serviced, computed after undoing the expensing of research; a firm generating large intangible-adjusted profits on a small base of debt and equity, while holding ample working capital, has both a real economic moat and the means to defend it.
considered.reasoning: This combines the two independent improvements discovered in gen 6 — the invested-capital denominator (fmb 3.01, alpha 3.3%) and the R&D adjustment (alpha 5.1%) — into a single profitability variable rather than an average of ranks, so it is a new measurement construct rather than a recombination of signals. Because operating liabilities are excluded from the denominator, the measure is not mechanically related to the working-capital quality leg it is paired with, keeping the interaction clean. All inputs are dense and the expression needs no time window.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Committed Research Programme Profits
considered.hypothesis: What distinguishes a genuine technological moat from discretionary spending is continuity: a firm that has run a research programme in every one of the last five years has an institutional commitment that competitors cannot replicate quickly, and profits defended by such a programme are durable provided the firm is not forced by maturing debt to interrupt it.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the SG&A test with a discrimination the archive can actually make — whether the gen-6 breakthrough comes from the *magnitude* of research intensity or from the *continuity* of the research commitment — and a reporting-persistence count cannot mechanically cancel against oibdp the way a spending ratio does, since a count is not an expense netted out of operating income. It is also free of the xsga-subsumes-xrd overlap the critic identified, because the count uses the R&D item directly and measures only its presence across years. Contrasted with the accepted knowledge-stock and intensity variants, the three together decompose the innovation channel into commitment, accumulated stock and current spending, which is exactly the diagnostic the final generation needs.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Intangible Capitalised Return On Assets
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: If research is genuinely an investment, then correcting the accounts requires adding the spending back to profit *and* adding the accumulated knowledge stock to the capital base; the resulting return on total (tangible plus intangible) capital is the economically correct profitability rate, and it is durable precisely when maturing debt cannot force the research programme to be cut.
considered.reasoning: The archive has tested the numerator correction (add-back, 4.33/4.9%) and the stock (as a separate ranked channel, 4.69/5.1%) but never the internally consistent capitalisation that puts both corrections in the same ratio, which is the specification implied by the expensing hypothesis and which also removes the double-counting of research-heavy firms that arises when the stock is ranked alongside profitability. Because the denominator grows with the knowledge stock, the measure no longer mechanically favours firms simply for spending, so it separates *productive* research franchises from expensive ones. Coverage is unaffected since non-researchers contribute zero on both sides.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Research Floor Backed Profits
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), TS_MIN(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 5))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: A moat is defended by the research the firm maintains in its worst year, not by its average or cumulative spend: firms that never let research intensity fall below a high floor have made the fixed commitment competitors must match, whereas firms that cut research when conditions tighten reveal that the spending was discretionary.
considered.reasoning: The count measures whether research happened and the stock measures how much accumulated, but neither measures the sustained *rate*, and a five-year minimum of research intensity is the sharpest available test of the commitment interpretation that the funding-safety interaction implies. It complements the accepted variants rather than duplicating them, since a firm can score high on cumulative spend while having slashed intensity recently. Zero-filling remains correct: a genuine non-researcher has a floor of zero.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Knowledge Stock And Safe Funding Only
considered.hypothesis: If accumulated research capital combined with freedom from refinancing pressure is itself the durable-strength signal, then current accounting profitability adds nothing and may even subtract, because reported profit is depressed by exactly the investment that creates the future franchise.
considered.reasoning: This is the attribution experiment the final generation needs: every strong signal in the archive contains a profitability level leg, so we do not know whether that leg still contributes once the knowledge stock is present or whether it is merely along for the ride. A result near the 5.1% parent would show that the innovation-plus-safety pair carries the information and that the last generation should optimise those two legs; a clear drop would confirm that current profitability remains essential and that the composite structure is correct. Inputs are dense and the construction is deliberately minimal.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Corrected Profit Full Funding Safety
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)), RANK(SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt)), RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Research programmes are threatened both by debt that must be refinanced and by an absence of liquid resources to fund the next development cycle, so the intangible-adjusted profitability of a firm protected on both dimensions should be the most durable of all.
considered.reasoning: When innovation profitability was paired with working-capital buffers alone the alpha held at 4.9% but the cross-sectional slope collapsed to 1.60, whereas the maturity leg delivers slopes above 4.3; combining them equally weighted tests whether liquidity adds abnormal return without destroying the slope, which is precisely the joint-evidence trade-off the objective cares about. The profitability leg is the arithmetically clean add-back rather than a rank blend, so any change is attributable solely to the quality composite. Inputs are dense and no window is needed.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Corrected Profit Against Hard Claims
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(oibdp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), lt))))
considered.hypothesis: What endangers a research franchise is the presence of enforceable financial claims of any maturity, not merely those due within the year, because long-dated debt still imposes covenants and interest that force discretionary spending cuts in a downturn; the enforceability of claims, rather than their timing, may be the binding constraint.
considered.reasoning: The hard-versus-soft-claims leg produced the best cross-sectional slope of any balance-sheet leg (3.31) but only 1.7% alpha when paired with raw profitability, and the natural diagnosis is that the profitability leg was too weak to exploit it; pairing it with the intangible-corrected profit leg is a clean one-change test of whether that diagnosis is right. Together with Signal 5 it completes the quality-leg map for the strongest profit measure — short-dated debt, all financial debt, and debt plus liquidity — which is exactly what the final generation needs to lock in the best combination. Coverage is at the archive maximum.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Self Financed Knowledge Capital
considered.hypothesis: A moat built with owners' money is safer than one built with creditors' money: a firm that has accumulated a large stock of research capital while keeping its total obligations small has financed its competitive position from internal profits, so no creditor can force it to abandon that position, whereas an equally research-heavy firm with a large claim stack has effectively pledged its moat.
considered.reasoning: Rather than stacking two tested R&D proxies on the profitability side, this puts research capital and total claims into a single scale-free quantity on the quality side, so the interaction being tested is the *financing source* of the intangible base rather than the timing of the debt that happens to sit against it. It is distinct from the archived knowledge-stock signal, which scaled the stock by assets and conditioned separately on short-term debt: here a firm with a large research base and heavy long-term obligations is penalised, which the parent does not do. Inputs are dense, the zero-fill convention remains economically correct for non-researchers, and the five-year window has cost this archive no coverage.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Conjunctive Profit Knowledge Safety
considered.expression: MUL(MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Durable operating strength requires all three attributes at once — the firm must actually earn profits today, own an accumulated research base that defends them tomorrow, and owe nothing soon that could force it to liquidate either; a firm missing any one of the three should not sit in the long leg.
considered.reasoning: Every innovation signal in the archive averages profitability and research inside a SUMRANK, which lets an extreme R&D rank carry unprofitable firms into the top bucket — the precise mechanism that produced a 5.7% alpha with a 1.45 slope when profitability was removed entirely. Replacing the additive blend with a conjunction forces the long leg to satisfy the profitability condition as well, which should restore the strong Fama-MacBeth slope while retaining the research-driven abnormal return. This is an economically motivated change of the conjunction logic rather than a new ingredient, and coverage is unchanged at the archive maximum.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Corrected Profit Self Financed Moat
considered.hypothesis: A moat financed by owners rather than creditors is the durable kind: a firm with high intangible-adjusted profitability that has accumulated its research base while keeping total claims small owns its competitive position outright, so neither the profits nor the research programme is contingent on credit conditions.
considered.reasoning: This unites the archive's two highest-Sharpe elements — the expensing-corrected profit leg (0.302) and claim-scaled knowledge capital (0.369, slope 4.08) — with a single controlled change from Self Financed Knowledge Capital, namely correcting the profitability numerator that R&D spending mechanically depresses. Because the quality leg scales research capital by total liabilities rather than assets, the interaction penalises heavily indebted researchers, which the maturity-based signals do not, giving a distinct portfolio composition and the best chance of high risk-adjusted return. Inputs are dense and no additional window is introduced.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Innovation Bonus For Safe Firms
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), MUL(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at), INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt)), -0.1)))
considered.hypothesis: Profitability is priced across the whole cross-section, but investors additionally underprice the accumulated research base of firms that are free of refinancing pressure, because only those firms can be confident of carrying the programme to commercial fruition; research capital at rollover-dependent firms deserves no such premium.
considered.reasoning: Every innovation signal so far is a pure rank product, which discards the profitability main effect and therefore trades slope against alpha; this specification keeps the full profitability ordering in the first channel and adds a knowledge-stock credit only inside the funding-safe group, which is structurally different from anything in the innovation family and is the design that historically produced the archive's most stable portfolios (Sharpe 0.277–0.309 with full coverage). Because the interaction term is exactly zero for rollover-dependent firms, the signal implements the conditional-premium hypothesis literally rather than through a smooth product. Inputs are dense and the threshold is an economic cutoff on short-term debt share, not a fitted parameter.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Short Debt Against Illiquid Capital
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, ADD(SUB(at, act), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))))))
considered.hypothesis: Knowledge capital is the least saleable asset a firm owns, so a research-intensive company that funds itself with debt maturing inside a year is running the most acute form of asset-liability mismatch: the assets backing the debt cannot be liquidated at all, and a refinancing failure destroys the franchise rather than merely shrinking it.
considered.reasoning: The flagged version was numerically dominated by current assets and therefore collapsed onto the already-tested working-capital leg; this instead scales short-term debt by the illiquid asset base, tangible plus intangible, so the leg is a genuine mismatch measure and rises only when maturing debt is large relative to assets that cannot be sold. It extends the gen-5 maturity-mismatch construct (3.0% alpha with raw profitability) by recognising that for research firms the illiquid base includes accumulated R&D, which is exactly the interaction the innovation family implies but has never tested. Coverage is unaffected since all inputs are dense and the zero-fill convention is unchanged.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Franchise Strength Three Channels
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), SUMRANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at), RATIO(oiadp, sale)))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: A durable franchise rests on three separable pillars — capital productivity, an accumulated knowledge base, and pricing power in the product market — and only a firm strong on all three, and free of refinancing pressure, has operating strength that competitors cannot erode.
considered.reasoning: The critic is right that the R&D stock and the R&D floor are monotone in the same underlying intensity, so the third channel here is operating margin, which is economically and statistically distinct: it delivered 3.9% alpha with a 1.22 slope in isolation, the mirror image of the asset-scaled profitability leg's profile, indicating low overlap rather than redundancy. Adding pricing power rather than a second research statistic gives the composite genuine breadth while keeping the profitability side dominant at two of three channels, which protects the cross-sectional slope. All inputs are dense and no new window is introduced.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: Peer Profitability Knowledge Safety
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
considered.hypothesis: Asset-scaled profitability is largely determined by industry capital intensity, so the informative quantity is how profitable a firm is relative to its direct competitors; measuring the profit channel peer-relative while leaving the research and funding channels pooled should identify firms that are genuinely out-earning rivals behind a defended, safely financed position.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the window tweak the critic correctly called cosmetic and instead makes the one conditioning change never applied to the archive's best signal — industry-adjusting the profitability channel alone; the earlier peer-relative test adjusted the R&D leg instead, which is a different experiment and one that weakened the result. Because sector effects in profit margins are exactly what dilute a pooled profit rank, this targets the slope side of the joint objective while leaving the alpha-generating research and maturity legs untouched. Coverage is unchanged at the archive maximum and no additional data items are required.
considered.author: proposer

critic_notes.rationale: This is essentially the well-documented earnings-volatility/earnings-stability anomaly repackaged as a profitability information ratio, and the construction is mechanically fragile because a negative mean ROA divided by a tiny volatility produces huge negative outliers while a loss-making but stable firm and a profitable but stable firm are scored on incomparable scales.

This is a straight additive rank blend of two of the most heavily published anomalies (Novy-Marx operating profitability and Sloan total accruals) with no genuine conditioning or interaction, so it mostly rediscovers known effects rather than testing a new cross-theme mechanism.

The binary gate does not implement the stated hypothesis — instead of making profitability "not count" for fragile firms, it forces every firm failing the working-capital test to the absolute bottom of the score, so the short leg becomes a pure low-liquidity/distress portfolio and the signal is largely a solvency indicator wearing a profitability label.

The economic story is reasonable but the multiplicative form on a signed, unbounded ROA is broken at the zero crossing — chronic loss-makers get a count of zero and therefore a score of exactly 0, ranking them above firms with mildly negative smoothed ROA and some profitable years, which inverts the intended ordering in the short leg.

Both legs lean on known effects (profitability trend and retained-earnings-to-assets), but the pairing is a coherent and non-obvious validation mechanism, the rank aggregation keeps scales comparable and coverage broad, and the expected positive sign matches the expression's natural direction.

critic_notes.target_name: Interest Adjusted Profit With Debt Coverage
critic_notes.rationale: The two-rank product is well-behaved and the interest-adjusted profit crossed with cash-flow debt coverage is a defensible cross-theme construct, though the reasoning's appeal to the "levered-ROE illusion" is inconsistent with an asset-scaled numerator and the second leg partially duplicates the profitability channel it is supposed to validate.

A rank product of high operating profitability and low leverage is essentially the profitability-plus-safety core of the published Quality-Minus-Junk construction, so it rediscovers two well-known standalone anomalies with a trivial multiplicative wrapper rather than testing a new interaction.

critic_notes.target_name: Profits Not Propped By New Debt
critic_notes.rationale: Conditioning smoothed profitability on the *flow* of debt financing is a coherent and mechanically consistent interaction that goes beyond the level-based leverage gate, though the low-debt-growth leg alone overlaps heavily with the documented debt-issuance/financing anomaly, so the incremental content hinges on the interaction actually paying off.

The construction is internally consistent and well-scaled, but the stated motivation ("graded repair of the gen-0 binary solvency gate") refers to a signal not present in the archive, and the long leg's preference for high net working capital runs against the documented negative pricing of working-capital/net-operating-asset levels, which should be flagged as a sign risk rather than a fatal flaw.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archived "Improving Profits With Earned Capital" signal — same two ingredients with TREND swapped for its own level and SUMRANK swapped for MUL — and both legs (profitability, retained earnings/assets) are individually published anomalies, so it is an ablation dressed up as a new hypothesis.

The proposal explicitly describes itself as Piotroski-style and combines exactly the F-score's profitability, Δleverage and Δliquidity components, making it a direct rediscovery of a long-published anomaly; the nested SUMRANK also silently double-weights profitability relative to the two change legs.

The multiplicative operating-times-financial-leverage penalty is a genuinely distinct mechanism from single-dimension leverage conditioning and is monotone and bounded after ranking, but the expected sign puts the signal on a collision course with the documented positive operating-leverage premium (Novy-Marx), which should be treated as the key diagnostic if the slope comes out flat or wrong-signed.

critic_notes.target_name: Profit Coverage Of Near Term Claims
critic_notes.rationale: A clean, well-motivated single-ratio ablation of the two winning composites, and the industry adjustment is justified since current-liability intensity is sector-driven, though EBITDA-to-current-liabilities is close to standard distress/coverage screens (Beaver-style cash-flow-to-debt) and unwinding the rank-product may simply reintroduce the outlier sensitivity that ranking was there to control.

Internally consistent and a legitimate complementarity-versus-redundancy test of the two independently successful legs with equalized weighting, but it is an incremental merge of two archive winners whose result is likely to sit mechanically between the parents, so its diagnostic value hinges entirely on the leg correlation being reported alongside the alpha.

This is a cosmetic three-year-smoothing variant of the archive's best signal, and the archive already contains two cases where MA-smoothing the profitability leg (Profits Not Propped By New Debt, Stable Financing Durable Profits) collapsed alpha to roughly zero, so the prior on smoothing helping here is weak and the design choice has effectively been tested.

The stated mechanism is an externally priced implied borrowing rate, but xint/lt is dominated by the interest-bearing share of the liability stack rather than by the rate charged, so the expression largely recomputes the debt-mix channel already captured by dlc/lt while the hypothesis claims a distinct information source.

The conjunctive logic is coherent and the control is clean, but MIN of two uniform ranks is very highly correlated with their product, so this is a near-cosmetic functional-form variant of the parent with little expected incremental information and added tie/compression problems in the extreme buckets.

The sales-benchmarked current-liability growth leg is the batch's only genuinely new flow mechanism and is economically sensible, but note the direction contradicts the working-capital accrual anomaly (rising current liabilities lower accruals, which Sloan associates with higher future returns) and lct growth is strongly correlated with total asset growth, so the test must control for both to be interpretable.

The stated distinction is spurious because oibdp is definitionally close to sale − cogs − xsga, so this is a near-tautological restatement of the archive's existing "Rollover Risk Adjusted Profitability" winner dressed up as a cleaner-profit hypothesis (and the numerator is itself the published Novy-Marx operating profitability factor).

Replacing dlc/lt with dlc/act is an economically substantive change (self-retirement capacity rather than claim composition) that unifies the two independently successful quality legs into one comparison, the sign convention is internally consistent, and inputs are dense — though it will be highly correlated with a plain current-ratio/liquidity screen and thus with the existing gen-2 composite.

The construction is a mechanical splice of two already-evaluated archive signals, and the counted condition (annual EBITDA exceeding total current liabilities) is a bar most firms never clear, so the five-year count risks being degenerate at zero for the bulk of the cross-section and mainly picking up asset-light industry membership rather than persistence.

Double industry-neutralization of the winning rank-product is a legitimate and cheap conditioning-set test whose stated motivation (sector rather than firm selection driving the legs) is coherent, but it is a wrapper on an existing signal rather than a new mechanism, so its upside is limited to a robustness verdict.

This is the batch's only genuine single-quantity interaction of the two themes — cash-flow variability scaled by near-term claims as a crude distance-to-distress — it is dimensionally coherent and sign-consistent, and it is distinct from the archive's failed capital-structure-volatility attempt, though it will partly overlap the known earnings-volatility anomaly.

A first difference of the winning quality leg is a mechanical rather than conceptual innovation and overlaps known debt-maturity/net-debt-issuance anomalies, but the flow-versus-level question is cleanly posed, the sign is consistent, and a null result is genuinely informative for closing off flow variants.

critic_notes.target_name: Dual Profit Measure With Term Funding
critic_notes.rationale: This is essentially the average of two already-tested signals that share the identical NEG(dlc/lt) quality leg, so the expected gain is a rank-averaging smoothing artifact rather than new economic content, and the "complementary measurement error" story is asserted rather than tested.

The worst-case TS_MAX operator is a legitimate and sign-consistent reframing of the archive's best quality leg, but because dlc/lt is highly persistent the five-year maximum will be strongly collinear with the already-tested level, limiting incremental information.

Coherent and correctly signed consolidation of the two strongest archive quality legs, though the claim of near-orthogonality is overstated since both legs are built from current assets and current liabilities, and one leg is a coarse 0–5 count that will contribute mostly ties.

EBITDA-to-total-debt is a standard credit metric that is close to a rediscovery of the profitability-plus-low-leverage quality composite, and because both legs share oibdp in the numerator the "interaction" largely double-counts profitability rather than isolating debt capacity, with low- and zero-debt firms driving the extreme ranks even after winsorising.

The re-scaling of EBITDA volatility to assets is a genuine diagnosis-driven fix of the archive's size-contaminated volatility leg, and the additive SUMRANK correctly implements the stated substitutability of stability and funding safety, though the result will sit close to conventional quality/low-earnings-volatility exposure.

The industry-neutralisation is a defensible targeted response to the margin signal's high-alpha/low-slope/low-Sharpe pathology, but simultaneously swapping the liquidity leg from dlc/lt to dlc/act makes it a three-way recombination of existing archive entries whose attribution will be ambiguous, and the archive already showed IND_RANK did not improve the asset-scaled version.

This uses the identical three legs and identical inputs as the archived "Funding Pressure Adjusted Profitability" (fmb 3.12, alpha 4.0%) with only the aggregation operator swapped from SUMRANK to a rank product, which is a cosmetic re-specification rather than a substantively different mechanism, and rank products of correlated quality legs behave very similarly to rank sums in the extreme buckets.

The cash-based profitability leg is a well-known published anomaly (Ball et al. cash operating profitability) and the rollover-risk leg is already the archive's workhorse, so the contribution is a single-leg substitution rather than a new mechanism, but the substitution is economically motivated (claims are settled in cash, not accruals), internally consistent in sign, and the coverage risk is correctly identified as the key diagnostic.

Because both legs share the sales denominator, the rank product is close to a monotone decomposition of oiadp/lct — i.e. essentially the already-tested "Profit Coverage Of Near Term Claims" (fmb 2.00, alpha 0.6%, negative Sharpe) — so the stated novelty of "dimensional consistency" is precisely what collapses it back onto a prior weak result.

Scaling short-term debt by the illiquid (non-current) asset base is a genuinely distinct normalisation from the archive's dlc/lt and dlc/act, the maturity-mismatch mechanism is coherent and sign-consistent with the expression, and the main hazard (near-zero non-current assets for asset-light firms) is acknowledged and largely neutralised by the rank transform.

Replacing the persistent profitability level with its one-year change is a legitimate and diagnostically informative test of whether the family is a static quality tilt or genuinely conditions news, though profitability changes are themselves a documented anomaly and the far lower autocorrelation of the flow leg makes a weakened alpha the likely outcome.

The gate is internally inconsistent with its own hypothesis because dlc is already a component of lct, so act − (lct + dlc) double-counts short-term debt rather than measuring "liquid resources exceeding every near-term claim," and stripped of that framing it is a threshold tweak to the archived gen-4 "Profitability Plus Safe Firm Premium" specification.

critic_notes.target_name: Profit State And News Safely Funded
critic_notes.rationale: This is an average of two already-tested signals against the identical maturity leg — level×NEG(dlc/lt) (alpha 4.0%, t=3.55) and delta×NEG(dlc/lt) (alpha 3.3%, t=3.03) — so the expected result is mechanically bracketed by its two parents, and the outer RANK around SUMRANK is a redundant monotone wrapper; it is a cosmetic recombination rather than a new economic hypothesis.

An untested pairing of two archive legs whose diagnostic purpose (does the profit-change leg need maturity safety specifically or generic slack?) is legitimate and the expression matches the hypothesis, but it remains leg-swapping within a saturated family and both parents' alphas set a low ceiling on incremental information.

The stated coverage defence is incorrect — SUMRANK needs both inputs, so the sparse oancf leg (0.08 in the gen-0 test) will bind the whole signal's coverage rather than being cushioned by the dense maturity leg, and the likely outcome is the archive's best-performing leg diluted and its sample halved, which is uninterpretable as evidence about cash-based safety.

The construction is internally consistent and the argument that a ratio-change captures both numerator and denominator improvement is fair, but the two legs share oibdp so a large part of the product is a squared profitability term, and the deleveraging channel it adds resembles "Profits Not Propped By New Debt," which produced negative alpha.

R&D intensity is a genuinely new channel for this archive and the funding-safety interaction is economically coherent, but xrd/sale is a long-published anomaly proxy, COALESCE-to-zero creates a large tied mass at the bottom of the rank, and R&D intensity is negatively correlated with contemporaneous oibdp/at so the SUMRANK may partly cancel the profitability leg it is meant to reinforce.

Unlike the rest of the batch this fuses the liquidity and debt legs into a single scale-free net-financial-position quantity rather than averaging ranks, giving it a distinct functional form and a monotone economic interpretation, though it is close to the standard net-debt construct and its incremental value over the existing NWC/lt leg (alpha 4.1%) is uncertain.

A clean, internally consistent measurement correction (since Compustat's oibdp is net of xrd via xsga, the add-back is arithmetically valid) that directly tests whether the gen-6 breakthrough is an expensing artefact rather than a two-anomaly blend, though it edges toward the well-documented intangible-adjusted-profitability literature.

Economically coherent and diagnostically useful, but it is only a funding-leg swap between two legs already extensively tested in the archive, so it is a recombination rather than a new construct and its incremental information is limited to which quality dimension dominates.

Replacing the R&D flow with a five-year knowledge stock is a defensible and standard refinement (close to the known R&D-capital anomaly), but the stated justification is internally wrong — scaling the stock by `at` creates a shared denominator with the oibdp/at profitability leg rather than breaking one — and undepreciated cumulative spend mostly re-ranks the same firms as current intensity.

The test cannot discriminate what it claims, because xsga in Compustat generally subsumes xrd (so the SG&A leg partly reproduces the R&D leg mechanically) while simultaneously suffering the exact cancellation problem the author criticised in the parent — oibdp is computed net of xsga, so ranking profitability and SG&A intensity together offsets — and organisation-capital-from-SG&A is itself a published anomaly.

A legitimate and well-motivated sector-bet diagnostic for a leg known to be heavily industry-clustered, but it is a robustness variant of the parent rather than a new mechanism, and its main value is confirmatory rather than exploratory.

The intangible-adjusted return-on-financed-capital numerator is a genuinely new measurement construct, but the proposal changes three things at once relative to the breakthrough (R&D add-back, invested-capital denominator, and a swap of the funding leg from debt maturity to working capital), so any result will be uninterpretable as to which change drove it.

This is the internally consistent capitalisation the expensing hypothesis actually implies (add-back in both numerator and capital base), it is not a duplicate of either the numerator-only or stock-as-separate-rank archive entries, and it usefully removes the mechanical tilt toward heavy spenders — though the reviewer should expect it to *weaken* results if the archive's gains came from that tilt rather than from productivity.

This is "Committed Research Programme Profits" with xrd added back to the profit leg, i.e. two already-tested, same-channel R&D proxies (add-back and continuity count) stacked on the same side of the composite, so it is a cosmetic recombination whose outcome is close to mechanically implied by the two parent results.

A five-year minimum of research intensity is a genuinely different statistic from the count or the cumulative stock and directly operationalises the "commitment" claim, but with COALESCE zero-filling the floor collapses to zero for any firm with a single gap year, so in practice the leg will be a heavily tied near-binary variable highly correlated with the already-tested TS_COUNT version.

critic_notes.target_name: Knowledge Stock And Safe Funding Only
critic_notes.rationale: As a deliberate ablation it is the right attribution test and is honestly framed, but on its own R&D-to-assets is a long-published anomaly, so a strong result would be substantially a rediscovery rather than a new cross-theme finding.

A clean one-change test of whether the liquidity leg can be added to the maturity leg without collapsing the Fama-MacBeth slope, but it is close to "Funding Pressure Adjusted Profitability" with only the R&D add-back swapped in, so the incremental information over the two parents is modest.

The stated diagnosis — that the hard-claims leg's strong slope but weak alpha reflected a weak profitability partner — is testable and the substitution is a single controlled change, but the whole batch now consists largely of permutations around the same ~5% alpha family and the marginal payoff from further leg-swapping is diminishing.

A legitimate functional-form test (conjunctive triple product versus the archive's compensatory SUMRANK) with a clear diagnostic motivation, though it is a close relative of Knowledge Stock Backed Profits and the triple rank product compresses discrimination, so the likely outcome is a firmer slope at the cost of the R&D-driven alpha.

Because act is typically several times dlc, NEG((dlc-act)/lt) is numerically dominated by act/lt and is therefore close to the working-capital-to-liabilities leg already tested in Working Capital Backed Profitability and Net Liquid Position After Debt, so the stated "net rollover pressure" interpretation does not match what the expression actually ranks.

The five-year R&D stock and the five-year minimum R&D/sales are both monotone functions of sustained research intensity and will rank firms very similarly, so nesting them mainly halves the effective weight on the profitability leg rather than adding a separable "continuity" dimension; the divergence in parent slope/alpha statistics is weak evidence of low correlation.

A clean one-change test on Self Financed Knowledge Capital with a coherent owner-financed-moat story, but xrd now enters both legs (current spend in the numerator, five-year sum in the quality leg), so part of the "interaction" is a mechanical R&D-squared term rather than a genuine profitability-times-safety conjunction.

The stated repair does not follow from the expression: the tie mass at zero comes overwhelmingly from COALESCE-zeroed non-reporters, whose three-year minimum is still exactly zero, so shortening the window is a cosmetic parameter tweak on the best-alpha archive signal rather than a fix to the degeneracy it claims to address.

Structurally distinct from the archive's pure rank products — it preserves the profitability main effect and applies the conditional premium to knowledge capital rather than to profitability, which is a real content change over Profitability Plus Safe Firm Premium — with the caveat that all rollover-dependent firms tie at zero in the bonus channel.
